verdict.rationale: Isaac Sim gives you the pieces for automated simulation testing. It can be integrated into existing testing and validation pipelines and used to automate workflows. It supports software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop evaluation, runs in Docker for repeatable setups, and offers headless and standalone scripted operation, pip-installable packages, and ROS 2 services to load worlds and step simulations. However, the evidence never shows a documented CI integration or a regression-testing workflow, so the developer must assemble the pipeline from these parts. missing for 10: explicit CI integration docs or examples (e.g., GitHub Actions/GitLab runners), a first-party regression-test framework or pass/fail harness, independent or hands-on corroboration of sim-based CI use.
